title: Doing life together Part 2
scripture_text: ‘’My command is this: Love each other as I have loved you. Greater love has no one than this: to lay down one’s life for one’s friends. You are my friends if you do what I command. I no longer call you servants, because a servant does not know his master’s business. Instead, I have called you friends, for everything that I learned from my Father I have made known to you. You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you so that you might go and bear fruit—fruit that will last—and so that whatever you ask in my name, the Father will give you. This is my command: Love each other.’’
devotional:
Friendships are essential for spiritual growth.

When Jesus chose these men to be his friends he chose them with the intention that their lives would become more fruitful. ‘You did not choose me, but I chose you and appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last.’

Within loving, healthy, sacrificial friendships is the ground where people grow most. Growth happens in the context of feeling loved, secure and accepted. It is where a person’s life can mature and bear fruit. If something happens within the relationship to cause us to feel insecure, growth and maturity is hindered if not prevented.

There is a statement at the end of verse 16 that is often overlooked, ‘’Then the father will give you whatever you ask in my name.’’ Six times during this last night with his disciples Jesus talks about praying in his name. I find the implications of what Jesus is saying here staggering. Often we hear people saying ‘in Jesus name’ at the end of their prayers as if it is the key that unlocks the answer to whatever you have been praying for. But I don’t think that that is what Jesus meant when He said this. He is tying together how we live and what we will pray for. If we become the kind of friends Jesus wants us to be, the natural consequence of that kind of living is that we will pray in Jesus’ name, i.e. we will be asking the Father the same things Jesus would be asking for, because we are endeavouring to love each other the way he loves us. It means that our prayers will be shaped by the character of Jesus that is being formed in us.

In his book Quality Friendships, Gary Inrig asks a number of searching questions about friendship.

a. What are the limits of my friendships? Do I use people or do I lay down my life for them? How much do I know of sacrificial love?

b. What is my impact on others? Am I a change agent for godliness in my friend’s life? Is he/she more of a disciple because of me? Am I giving myself in such a way that God-given needs are being met in his/her life?

c. Do I take the risk of openness, or is there a carefully constructed wall around my life that no one can penetrate? Have I ever expressed verbally my love and appreciation for my friend and displayed that love by opening up my life to them?

d. Am I an initiator of love, or am I waiting for others to earn my approval or to reach out to me? Do I choose my friends because of my needs or because of their needs?

e. How am I helping my friend realise his/her full potential in any or every area of their life? Is he/she fruitful because of me?
prayer: Father help to recognise and remember that there a link between my friendships and prayer life.
